description: MCP-style descriptions and JSON Schemas only; existing action/read wire is retained. This catalog is not an MCP server and grants no tool permissions.

materialization.read_snapshot: Replace snapshot_sha256 schema with const=current public observation hash, preserving type/pattern.
materialization.read_tokens: Replace all read.output_tokens.maximum with min(61440, policy.body_max_tokens).
materialization.tab_focus: Set index.maximum to current tab count-1; no empty ready tab set.
materialization.availability: Only task.allowed_actions and actually registered observation tools; never expose unavailable capabilities.
materialization.response_envelope: Rebuild read oneOf from the same materialized tool schemas; omit the read branch if no read tools are registered.
not_schema_checks: region existence, current snapshot/attempt binding and available captured row/codepoint range
cursor provenance and identical request parameters; only current-reader input mistake is correctable
UTF-8/finite numeric values and strict JSON integer representation, no booleans-as-integers or string coercion
current authority, claim, cancellation, dispatch budget and existing once ledgers
remaining read quota and continuous invalid-proposal limits from existing trace; no independent ledger

suggested_new_invalid_policy.status: Proposed successor defaults; identical count includes the first rejected proposal. Existing frozen runs and installed policy remain unchanged until new acceptance.
suggested_new_invalid_policy.fingerprint: current observation reference + branch/tool + canonical original proposal arguments + specific rejection code; exclude thought, generation/request IDs and feedback text; preserve list order and Unicode literals
suggested_new_invalid_policy.reset: Retain the existing trace-derived consecutive-invalid streak and fingerprint algorithm. A valid dispatched read/action clears the streak and its repeated counts; snapshot change ends same-snapshot repeats. Within one streak and snapshot, the first identical rejection counts as 1, the second remains correctable, and the third stops before the next generation. Permission, unknown and once boundaries are never reset.

prompt_publication.single_source: Keep the complete catalog on the program side. Render compact model-facing definitions from the same schemas; never send this handoff file wholesale.
prompt_publication.fixed_system: One system message per logical request, built once per enabled-tool/policy/prompt version. Retain names, purpose, argument types, required/default/enum/effective constraints and material effects. Factor shared read fields once. State that colons in signatures denote types; Python action keyword arguments use name=value. Do not include a full example for every tool.
prompt_publication.dynamic_user: Current snapshot, tabs, public regions and necessary corrective feedback; current-bound format examples appear once here. Omit the routine Current proposal state block and quota/invalid-proposal/no-progress counters. Read reminders start at frozen policy.warn_remaining and persist thereafter: select 3 for this candidate; a larger quota may explicitly select 5, below the total read quota. Do not wait until only 1 read remains. Keep counters internal; show rejection-specific correction and a short notice near the stop limit. The framework enforces exhaustion/stop limits and omits further read examples when exhausted. Keep observations/history bounded; never append previous full requests.
prompt_publication.model_schema_split: Frozen max_ranges and body_max_tokens may be rendered in the fixed contract. Current snapshot const and tab maximum stay in dynamic facts and program-side per-request validation. Do not print changing snapshots inside the fixed system.
prompt_publication.examples: Keep one complete enabled browser-action example, preferring click when a suitable public bid exists, plus one concise example per registered and still-available read tool (at most three). On a correctable rejection use one tool/error-specific complete example and replace its ordinary example rather than duplicating it. Full per-tool examples and correction templates remain program-side; bind public values before publication.
prompt_publication.wire_compatibility: Each independent messages request still carries its fixed system. No new native tools envelope or action format. A session/cache reference is usable only with explicitly implemented and validated backend semantics.
prompt_publication.cache_status: Read baseline uses one system plus one user and per-call generate(use_cache=True), without cross-request past_key_values. OpenRouter sends messages without explicit cache-control/session support; provider automatic hits are unverified.
prompt_publication.cache_accounting: Cached prefix tokens remain in the logical context limit. Track full input tokens, actual cache read/write tokens if returned, prefill latency and billed cost separately. Never replay a dispatched/unknown/returned request for cache measurement.
prompt_publication.scope: Compact contracts and single-prefix reuse first. Do not require a new cache service, stateful API migration or cross-job KV platform for this repair.

feedback_rendering.language: Render once in the current Actor prompt language; do not duplicate bilingual feedback.
feedback_rendering.coverage: Every enabled catalog tool has a correction template and a complete wire example. Combine the shared error code/field facts with this tool template; do not send the entire catalog.
feedback_rendering.binding: Use only verified current public IDs, ranges, snapshots, tabs, options, URLs, permitted files and observed answer facts. Validate the bound example with the actual parser/validator. If binding is unavailable, label a non-executable format template explicitly instead of inventing values or claiming full validity.
feedback_rendering.error_specificity: The example must include the corrected field, including optional parameters. Type/schema examples are not proof of authority, action appropriateness or business correctness.
feedback_rendering.persistence: Use existing next_action for the short correction and example; preserve the feedback schema, complete original exception and original response. Next-prompt rendering and independent review must use the same versioned deterministic rules.
feedback_rendering.deduplication: Publish one corrective example in the rejection block and suppress its same-branch/tool normal example in this request. Keep older rejection history bounded without accumulating old examples; retain original trace evidence.
feedback_rendering.stop_and_execution: Only confirmed pre-dispatch input errors use executed=false and corrective examples. At the third identical rejection record the terminal reason and do not make a fourth generation for that streak. No continue-reading example after quota exhaustion; no example enabling a forbidden tool. Preserve attempted action outcomes and stop on authority, integrity, cancellation or unknown failures.
feedback_rendering.size_target: Aim for <=350 native tokens per correction block, including the example; this is a drafting target, not a new runtime admission gate. Do not truncate valid JSON, required bounds or observations.
feedback_rendering.near_stop_notice: After the second identical rejection, say: Another identical invalid proposal will stop this run. Omit routine counter dumps.
feedback_rendering.unknown_tool: Use one actually enabled response-envelope example when the submitted tool cannot be identified; do not invent a callable name or silently substitute an operation.
